Lifecycle and installed software for every device, cooling modelled alongside power, application flows and maps, PRTG monitoring, floor plans grown into a building tool, a Routing tab on the topology, PDF reports, deploy pipelines, SBOMs, RPKI and MACsec, faster big lists and a long list of security and correctness fixes.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Upgrade note: prefixes whose CIDR isn't an address are deleted.**
> The upgrade adds a database index that reads every prefix's CIDR as an address. A prefix holding anything else (for example `banana` or `10.0.0.0/33`) would make the index build fail and roll the whole upgrade back. To prevent that, migration `api.0265_drop_unparseable_prefixes` runs first. It deletes every prefix Postgres can't read as an address and logs each one to the upgrade log as a `danbyte.migrations` warning, with its id, value and tenant.
>
> **This is unlikely to delete anything.** A prefix should only ever hold a CIDR: Danbyte has validated prefix input since #47, and an earlier migration already turned bare addresses into host prefixes. Only junk values saved before that validation existed are affected, and those already broke prefix search and filters. If you want to be sure, take a backup before upgrading and check the upgrade log afterwards for `deleting prefix` lines.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **One root step after upgrading (systemd installs).** Root must re-render the nginx site from this release's bundle. The upgrade shows the step on its *After this upgrade* card, with the commands to download the bundle again (an upgrade from the app deletes the uploaded one). It brings two changes:
> - nginx serves the frontend's build files under `/assets/` itself, compressed and cached for a year. Until the step is done everything works, only without the caching.
> - nginx lets Danbyte frame its own pages (`X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`, `frame-ancestors 'self'`). Until the step is done the topology PDF report stays at *Drawing…*.
>
> If you manage nginx yourself, add the `/assets/` block and the `$danbyte_asset_cache` map from `deploy/nginx/danbyte.prod.conf.template`, change `DENY` to `SAMEORIGIN` and `frame-ancestors 'none'` to `frame-ancestors 'self'`. Docker installs need nothing.

> [!NOTE]
> **API scripts that read whole lists must page.** A list request without `page_size` now returns 100 rows and a `next` link instead of up to 10,000, and a `page_size` above 2,000 is cut to 2,000. Follow `next`. The web app and the Python SDK already do. See Behaviour changes.

### Behaviour changes

- **List endpoints answer 100 rows by default** (`API_PAGE_SIZE`) with a `next` link. A `page_size` above `API_MAX_PAGE_SIZE` (default 2,000) is cut to it. Pages above 1,000 rows are limited to two in flight per user, shared across all of the user's tokens, and a third answers 429 with `Retry-After`. An invalid paging setting, `API_PAGE_SIZE=0` included, stops the service at start.
- **List endpoints answer 400** for a sort column or facet they don't know, instead of ignoring it.
- **API tokens are capped per user:** at most `API_MAX_TOKENS_PER_USER` (default 25) unexpired tokens; creating one more answers 400 until one is revoked or expires.
- **Foreign ids are refused on writes.** An id on a writable relation that is unknown or belongs to another tenant is a 400 field error everywhere. Interface bulk add and bulk update resolve tag ids the same way and never create a tag from a name.
- **Notification channel credentials are write-only.** `GET /api/monitoring/channels/` no longer returns a Slack, Teams, Discord or webhook channel's `url` or a PagerDuty `routing_key`; it answers `url_set` and `routing_key_set`, like the Telegram `bot_token_set`. Sending a value in `config` still sets it. The upgrade moves stored values into the encrypted store and the upgrader restarts the services straight after.
- **A deactivated tenant's Outposts and syncs stop.** Its Outpost tokens are refused on every Outpost endpoint and the build download, its SSH Outposts are no longer driven, and its Windows, virtualization and Zabbix connections no longer sync; a job queued before the deactivation returns without running.
- **Rack placement checks cooling.** A rack with a cooling capability refuses liquid, hybrid or immersion hardware it does not take, including blades and modules installed into a device in it. Air-cooled gear goes in any rack, and racks without a capability take anything. Existing placements are kept and listed under **Mismatched cooling**.
- **Time bars colour by time left** against the warning window, not by percent used.
- **Tag names are unique** per tenant, ignoring case. Existing duplicates stay until you merge them on the Tags page.
- **Creating a catalog entry with a name already in use answers 400** on `name`, even with a different slug. Entries that already share a name can still be edited.
- **SSH host keys can't be edited:** `PUT` and `PATCH` answer 405, and the device is fixed after upload.
- **BGP address families have their own rows** on sessions and peer groups. The old `address_families` list stays as a view kept in step with them; existing lists are backfilled.
- **Floor plans belong to a site.** Every plan and stack names a site (backfilled); the location is optional, and a plan without one covers the whole site.
- **Container prefixes get no automatic gateway,** nor does a prefix with **Automatic gateway** turned off. Existing gateways are kept.
- **Software versions carry a source.** Existing versions are marked `virtualization` when an integration set them and `manual` otherwise. An integration never overwrites a manual or imported value.
- **Users, groups and permissions guard against lock-out.** Deactivating or deleting your own account, the last active superuser, a built-in group, the built-in Administrator grant, or the last group or grant through which you manage users is refused, single and bulk alike.
- **A weak password set by an admin or at bootstrap is refused** (#489).
- **Script export and import see only the scripts you can see.** Export used to include other people's private scripts.
- **DHCP scopes and DNS zones are export-only** in import/export; an import could never create them.
- **A single device name with a range in it,** like `x[1-3]`, is refused instead of saved as text, in the form and in CSV import.
- **Two templates in one bundle writing the same path** is an error instead of the second overwriting the first.
- **`/topology` is the saved views list;** the map is at `/topology/map`. Old links redirect with their parameters.
- **Compliance opens on Overview.** The Violations and Rules tabs keep their URLs and filters.
- **The Applications list opens in tree order,** a parent followed by its children.
- **Webhook and AWX deploy payloads include `run_id`.**
- **Sidebar:** DCIM is regrouped into Devices, Catalog, Racks & cabinets and Connections; a new **Software & lifecycle** section holds applications, application groups, lifecycle, end-of-life products and support contracts; Power is now **Power & cooling**, and Routing sits between it and Wireless. Links and permissions are unchanged.

### Lifecycle and software

- **#436 - Lifecycle page.** **Software & lifecycle → Lifecycle** lists every device and VM against its hardware, OS, support coverage and installed software end dates, soonest first, with window count chips, facets, deep links (`/lifecycle?source=coverage&window=90`), export and saved views. `GET /api/lifecycle/`.
- **#436 - One time bar for every end date.** Hardware, OS and coverage bars colour by time left. The OS bar uses the platform's dates or its endoflife.date cycle, and says which. VMs get an OS support row.
- **#436 - Next end of life column** on the Devices and Virtual machines lists, sorted by days left.
- **#436 - Applications catalog** of the software you run, in a domain → process → application tree with an optional end-of-life product. The application page shows its path, children with install counts, the groups it belongs to and an End of life card listing every cycle its installs run, with Change product, Remove and Refresh now.
- **#436 - Installed software.** Device and VM pages get a Software tab and an Overview card; cycles follow the version; import, export and the API cover it.
- **#436 - Application groups** such as *RDS* or *SCADA*: assign one to a device or VM and it gets one install per member; unassigning removes the installs it created and keeps edited ones. A member added later lands on every host.
- **#436 - Groups in the Ansible inventory.** `/api/inventory/ansible/` lists each host's `application_groups` and `applications`, and every assigned group becomes an inventory group `app_group_<slug>`.
- **#436 - Compliance includes software.** End-of-life status rules can opt in to failing a device or VM on its installed software.
- **#395 - Software target.** Platforms take a target version and devices and VMs a software version ("17.9.4a · target 17.9.5"), with list columns, a filter and a compliance check that fails anything off target.
- **#395 - ESXi version from vCenter** with Read host hardware on, never overwriting a typed version.
- **#451 - Where a version comes from.** The version's source (manual, SNMP, virtualization, Oxidized, import) and when an integration last set it show on the Overview. SNMP extracts it from `sysDescr` for IOS, IOS-XE, NX-OS, Junos and EOS, or by a per-platform pattern; `manage.py extract_software_versions` re-reads stored facts.
- **#451 - Versions view** on Lifecycle: version by platform with counts, on-target state and sources. `GET /api/lifecycle/versions/`, and `?software_version=` / `?software_version_source=` on the device and VM lists.
- **Device profiles** hand a device or VM its application groups, tags, platform and blank custom fields in one assignment and release them on unassign. A profile's page has *Add device* and *Assign devices*.
- **Custom end-of-life products** next to the catalog, and an **End-of-life products** list with filters, bulk edit, safe bulk delete and export.

### SBOM

- **#468 - SBOM for your inventory:** a CycloneDX 1.6 document of devices and VMs with their OS and installed software (name, version, supplier, licence, package URL and CPE with `{version}` / `{os_version}` templates). From the Devices and VMs lists with the current filters, the site page, or `GET`/`POST /api/sbom/` by site (id, name or slug), tag, role, device or VM. Components without a licence are counted, never guessed; sites you can't view are not named.
- **Licences:** applications and platforms have an SPDX licence; an install can override it.
- **Danbyte's own SBOM** ships with every release: `danbyte-<version>.cdx.json` on the release page, `sbom.cdx.json` in the bundle and image, and a download under **Settings → Updates**.

### Application flows and map

- **#163 - Application flows:** the traffic an application needs, from an address, range, prefix or any to another, by protocol and ports, with status and direction. Flows tabs on applications, devices, VMs, IP addresses and prefixes.
- **#163 - Application map:** a *Tree* view of the application hierarchy with its hosts and a *Flows* view with protocol and ports on each line, arrowheads by direction and colour by status. Filters, search, legend, detail panels and PNG, SVG, PDF and draw.io export. The application's Diagram tab embeds it.
- **Flow requirements:** an application states the flows it needs, with ends on its own hosts or another application's, and Danbyte keeps the generated flows in step with installs, addresses, hosts and services. Change-log entries gain a cause.

### Cooling

- **#434, #469 - Cooling on hardware and racks.** Device types, module types and devices record how they are cooled and their heat output; racks and rack types what their cooling takes and how much heat it removes. Heat load (blades and modules counted in their chassis' rack) against capacity shows on the rack page, the racks list, floor plans coloured by Cooling, the 3D rack card and the site Capacity tab, with filters for capability, free cooling, method and mismatch.
- **#434 - Cooling sources and feeds:** chillers, CRAHs and in-row coolers and the loops to racks, with capacity, flow and temperatures, lists, bulk edit, import/export and a rack's Cooling feeds tab. A rack without its own capacity is measured against its primary feeds.
- **#434 - Cooling intakes and outflows** on devices and device types, fed from a feed or a CDU, with the cooling path on the device overview (`/api/devices/{id}/cooling-path/`) and connected flow on the feed.
- **#434 - What a source takes down.** Power panels, power feeds, cooling sources and feeds get an Affected tab of downstream racks and devices, and Plan maintenance opens an event with those impacts filled in.
- **#434 - Airflow and power budget:** the device page shows effective airflow; rack types carry a power budget the rack form pre-fills.

### PRTG monitoring

- **Connection and status:** Settings → Integrations → **PRTG monitoring**, an encrypted write-only API key, **Test connection**, matching of PRTG devices to devices and VMs with a review queue for ties, an editable state map and a `prtg` check kind. A PRTG column and filter on the device and VM lists.
- **Sensors tab** on device and VM pages: one card per sensor, channel gauges with warning and error bands, lookup bars, sparklines and 1h/24h/7d history. Sensors link to the IP address, interface or service they poll and can be pinned to an Overview. `/prtg` lists sensors and alarms; two dashboard widgets.
- **Two-way:** acknowledging in either system acknowledges in the other; acknowledge, pause and resume from Danbyte; maintenance windows can pause linked devices; unmatched PRTG devices can be adopted; system information can feed inventory drift. Each is a per-connection switch.
- **Danbyte as the source of truth:** a Monitor in PRTG / Exclude choice per device and VM, policies that pick a sensor profile and group, group trees built from regions, sites, locations and roles, and per-device sensor overrides. Applying creates devices and sensors through API v2 (PRTG 26.2.120 or later; older servers copy a seed device). Danbyte never touches a device or sensor it did not create, except to move a linked device its policy places elsewhere, which is proposed like any other change.
- **Add sensors by hand** or run PRTG's discovery from the Sensors tab. Delete dialogs offer **Also remove from PRTG**, and retirement rules pause or delete PRTG devices by status or tag.
- **One monitoring card** on device and VM pages for Danbyte checks, Zabbix and PRTG.

### Floor plans and buildings

- **Rooms:** locations hold rooms; devices, racks and cabinets name their room. Rooms have their own list and page.
- **Floors and buildings:** stacks of floors with a switcher, aligned into one building with basements, a shared footprint and slab thickness. A level picker shows All, Up to or Only a level, with onion skin in 2D and the building floor by floor in 3D. A floor takes its stack's location when it has none.
- **Site-wide plans and the Site map:** a plan can cover a whole site, with a base map layer under each floor's own drawing (none for basements). An aligned building is one footprint on the Site map, named after it, listing its levels and opening the ground floor, as does an outline's drill-down. **Edit area** on the map grows or shrinks the plan's frame without moving anything placed, on all aligned levels at once; a trim that would cut something is refused naming what.
- **Areas, labels, walls, doors, trays and raised floors** drawn and edited on the plan. Area names stay readable on strong fills in both themes. Walls around an area stay linked both ways: editing a wall redraws the area in the same undo step and reshaping the area rebuilds its walls. **Detect outline** traces walls from the map, picture or drawing.
- **Raised floors as polygons,** drawn with the Polygon tool or made from an area; touching raised floors of one depth and colour draw as one pad in 2D, 3D and export.
- **Placing objects** from a picker with room checks and photos, free placement off the grid, and devices sized by their measured dimensions.
- **Cable routes** with computed lengths and tenant length rules, routed along trays and re-routed when tiles or trays move, drawn in lanes and bundles; **Connect to** plans new cables; risers carry cables between floors.
- **Crowded plans stay readable:** a row of racks is named once along it (`Row B · B01–B12`) and drawn as one bar when zoomed out, rooms fold into one summary further out, and infrastructure is summed per wall. Other names go to callouts with short leaders, or one summary plate (`RACK-01–RACK-07`) with a hover card and *Zoom to these*. Large plans stay smooth while zooming.
- **Cameras:** views stop at walls (doorways see through, racks optionally block) in 2D, 3D and PDF, reach goes past 50 cells, and **Display › Camera coverage** tints blind spots with the share of the floor seen, per area too.
- **3D:** an architectural look in both themes, GLB models for device types and devices with ports mapped, floor-placed devices, callouts, and plan labels and room, area, zone and tray names on each level's floor (Display toggles Labels and Room & area names).
- **Tiles** for power panels, power feeds and cooling sources pin their popover on a click, showing load against rating.
- **Panels and snapshots:** detail panel layouts per device type, role, profile or tenant under Settings → Floor plans; snapshots of a room, location or area.
- **Export:** the view, a room or area, a floor or a whole building as PDF with a cable schedule, inventory and ports. Exports use the same row names, callouts and summaries as the canvas.
- **Demo seeders, opt-in:** `make seed-floorplan-demo TENANT=<slug>` and `make seed-building-demo TENANT=<slug>`. Nothing is seeded on upgrade.

### Topology

- **Routing tab:** routers with router ID, ASNs and loopback in movable AS boxes; eBGP and iBGP sessions (route reflector arrows), OSPF and IS-IS adjacencies with areas, levels and costs, static routes to their next hop; a VRF picker and a checks chip for one-sided sessions, AS mismatches and OSPF/IS-IS mismatches. Exports to SVG, PNG, PDF and draw.io. `GET`/`POST /api/topology/routing/`.
- **#466 - Provider networks on the maps:** a node on the topology and a marker on the site map, with a line from each site's switch through its circuit.
- **Circuits between sites** drawn as one dashed line between the two devices, labelled and coloured by circuit type.
- **Names are never cut:** cards grow and wrap to fit, in the map and every export.
- **Routing labels never overlap:** each line's label sits where it is free along its own line, or shows on hover; labels every line in an AS box shares are said once in the legend. A router's card names each AS once.
- **Bendy lines keep their curve** with labels written along them; every cable end keeps its addresses, IPv6 first when room is short.
- **Bands:** cards per row and alignment per band, saved with the view; a line type per device and per band.
- **Role badges on photos**, and the legend lists only the role colours on the map.
- **Saved views list** at `/topology` with who made and last changed each view.

### PDF reports

- **#474 - PDF reports** of devices, prefixes and IP addresses from their pages, the lists' Import / Export menu and the bulk bar: columns in your order, grouping, a summary, one page per object with the sections you choose, badges in their colours, an optional cover page, chapters with a clickable contents, and a sensitivity label on every page when one is set. Prefix reports group by VRF and can list each prefix's addresses. Large reports run in the background, with a live estimate. API: `/api/devices/report/`, `/api/prefixes/report/`, `/api/ips/report/`.
- **Topology report:** saved views as one PDF with each diagram, its devices, addresses and cabling, or a ZIP with one PDF per view.
- **Sensitivity labels** catalog (Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted to start with), editable like statuses, with a tenant default. Tenants set their cover colours and image.
- Every time in a report and on topology, floor plan, rack and cabinet PDFs and spec sheets is in your timezone, with the zone named.

### Deploy pipelines and config

- **Pipelines** under Integrations: automation targets run one after another on a device or VM, a failed step stopping the rest unless set to carry on. A pipeline can be a device role's default, run on change, and be exported or imported as YAML. The deploy dialog picks a pipeline or a single target and offers *Dry run*; the run page shows each step's status, log and output files, with *Cancel run* and *Re-run*.
- **Scripts as deploy targets:** a Danbyte script that declares a `device_ids` parameter, linked from the deploy run.
- **Runners can report back:** `POST /api/deploy-runs/<id>/result/`, signed with the webhook target's secret; a step set to *Wait for result* waits up to its timeout. `manage.py seed_pipeline_demo --tenant <slug>` adds an opt-in demo.
- **File viewer** on the Config tab and for config context, drift, script logs and export template previews: file list with *Changed* / *Matches* / *Never pushed*, search, line numbers, wrap, copy and download, an outline with folding, unified or side-by-side diffs, and syntax colours for JSON, XML, YAML, INI, network configs and logs.
- **Several files from one template:** a target path ending in `/` writes one file per `{% file "name" %}…{% endfile %}` block, each with its own hash, drift and diff.
- **Local config context** on devices and VMs, merged last, and config contexts that match by tag.
- **Intended VMs** for provisioning: **Provision** sends one to an automation target under its own permission, and virtualization sync never overwrites, deletes or prunes it.

### Networking

- **RPKI caches** on BGP instances and `match rpki` on policy rules; **ROAs** with an RFC 8416 SLURM export (`GET /api/routing/roas/slurm/`).
- **MACsec** on interfaces: cipher, replay window and a keychain holding the MKA key, which never passes through the interface API.
- **BGP:** per-address-family settings, and maximum-prefix warning threshold, restart interval and warning-only, inherited from peer groups.
- **WireGuard** on tunnel terminations, **LAG** bond mode, hash policy and miimon, **policy routing** (ip rules, kernel tables, NAT out interface), **EVPN** DF preference and a **VXLAN** interface type.
- **Automatic gateway per prefix** can be turned off, for loopback and point-to-point blocks.
- **Proxmox SDN:** the sync reads zones and VNets (needs `SDN.Audit` on `/sdn`), NICs link to their VNet, cables get a Proxmox VNet field (copied from a `pve_vnet` interface custom field on upgrade), VNets with two NICs can become cables (off by default), and a source's **Network plan** downloads as JSON for a runner. Danbyte only reads from Proxmox.
- **DNS records to IPAM in bulk.**

### Compliance

- **Overview tab** with counts, a card per rule worst first, and Top offenders. `GET /api/compliance/summary/`.
- **Violations built for triage:** facets, grouping by rule, and Acknowledge, Snooze or Reopen with a note. Triage needs `compliancetriage.change`, which Administrator and Operator have. `POST /api/compliance/triage/`.
- **Rule builder:** object types, a scope and conditions, with counts as you build.

### Devices, cables and lists

- **#454 - Cable several ports without closing the form:** **Save and add another** moves both ends to the next free port; **Many at once** pairs ticked ports on two devices (`POST /api/cables/bulk-create/`).
- **Device name ranges:** `DK-RDS-[1-10]` creates every device in one go, all or nothing, at most 128. `POST /api/devices/bulk-create/`.
- **Bulk select on every list,** with export, bulk edit and safe bulk delete where a single page allows them, and Enable / Disable, Activate / Deactivate, Requeue and Cancel where those exist. Secrets are never exported. Devices and VMs gain bulk delete, VMs and platforms bulk edit.
- **Tags:** **Merge into…** on the Tags page, and duplicate names are flagged.
- **Every address on the IPs tab** of a device or VM, with an Assigned to column; VMs get an IPs tab.
- **Search results are links,** so they open in a new tab; wide tables keep their scrollbar at the bottom of the window.
- **Tasks** can be added from an object's Tasks tab and the calendar.
- `/api/ips/` and `/api/prefixes/` filter by tag; templates' `link_peer` includes the far port's `mac_address` and `mtu`.

### Performance

- **#479 - Fixes** the prefix list taking 30 s with 5,000 prefixes: grouped tables are paged.
- **#482, #483, #487 - Fixes** slow Devices, Interfaces, Cables and VMs lists: paged, sorted, filtered and faceted on the server, fetching only the table's fields, with no 10,000-row cap.
- **#480, #484 - Fixes** slow natural-order device and VM lists and prefix containment lookups with new indexes.
- **#478 - Fixes** the update check blocking workers when GitHub is slow; the release list is cached for 6 hours.
- **#481 - Fixes** a new database connection per request: web workers keep theirs for 60 s (`DB_CONN_MAX_AGE`).
- **#485 - Fixes** the frontend's files being revalidated on every page load (see the root step above).
- **#486 - Fixes** a session write on every request: the idle timeout is refreshed at most once a minute.
- **#488 - Fixes** several small costs: a smaller first page load, a cached import/export type list and fewer queries on the Devices page.
- **#455 - Fixes** a device or VM page counting its addresses in many queries.
- **#460 - Fixes** the SLA agreement list querying channels per row.
- **The dashboard** reads rollups only for the widgets on show (about 9.5 s to 0.4 s on a busy install), and device and VM pages draw at once from the list's row.

### Security

- **#452 - Fixes** a few API calls with a huge `page_size` blocking every worker. Pages are capped and large pages limited per user.
- **#457 - Fixes** each new API token bringing its own large-page slots; tokens are also capped per user.
- **#449 - Fixes** parallel password and two-factor guesses passing the lockout: each attempt is counted before it is checked.
- **#489 - Fixes** passwords set by an admin or at bootstrap skipping the password rules.
- **#490 - Fixes** HSTS and X-Frame-Options being sent twice with different values. nginx now owns them behind the proxy.
- **#491 - Fixes** signed-in API responses having no `Cache-Control`. They are now `private, no-store`.
- **#456 - Fixes** interface bulk add and bulk update accepting tag ids from another tenant; writable relations on other endpoints did the same.
- **#458 - Fixes** SSH host keys being movable to another device after upload.
- **#459 - Fixes** Zabbix and PRTG error text that could include the API key.
- **#453 - Fixes** floor plan tile links, site map rows, application flows, cooling intakes and coverage titles naming objects a site-scoped reader can't view. They show as Hidden.
- **#473 - Fixes** an interface's link peer naming a cable's far end on a site the user can't see.
- **#438, #448 - Fixes** counts that included rows the reader can't view: tenant, prefix, VRF, VLAN, route target, L2VPN, tag, contact, cluster, location, cabinet and floor plan counts, among others.
- **Fixes** notification channel webhook URLs and PagerDuty routing keys being readable by every viewer, including Read-only, and a failed test send echoing the webhook path. They are stored encrypted and never returned.
- **Fixes** the API schema being served from a cache filled before the permission check.
- **Fixes** floor plan cables showing to readers who could not view them.
- **Fixes** a tag page's Tagged objects count including other tenants.
- **Fixes** deleting a certificate issuer leaving its ACME account key in the secret store, in bulk deletes too.
- **#462 - Updates** vulnerable frontend development dependencies, and vite, launch-editor and follow-redirects in the development tooling.
- **Dependency security updates:** Django 5.2.19, Django REST framework 3.18, and new minimums for Pillow, PyJWT, cryptography, certifi (distrusted root removed), dnspython, pyasn1, brotli, msgpack and autobahn.

- **#447 - Fixes** list pages that a token client read only part of.
- **#445 - Fixes** the device form's Card lines heading toggling Name only when clicked; screen readers announce it as the group's name.
- **#461 - Fixes** unlabelled controls for screen readers; a test fails on new ones.
- **#470 - Fixes** the Jobs page content area being unreachable by keyboard; a list page's content area is a focusable region.

- **#476 - Fixes** the site map on portrait phones: the objects panel no longer covers the map and the toolbar stays on screen.
- **#477 - Fixes** the cramped calendar toolbar and compliance condition rows on phones.
- **#475 - Fixes** a monitoring test that failed between 00:00 and 01:00 UTC.
- **Fixes** a catalog entry with a name already in use being saved under a new slug.
- **Fixes** VM custom fields not being validated on a single save.
- **Fixes** a new floor plan from a Location page saving without its site.
- **Fixes** text overflowing the rack card in the 3D floor plan.
- **Fixes** turned tiles on free-layout plans sitting at the wrong angle or size in 3D and in SVG/PDF export.
- **Fixes** a 3D view failing to open after a deploy replaced its files; it reloads once.
- **Fixes** floor plan tiles linked to a power panel or feed opening its edit form instead of its page, and `?cluster_site=` on the power panel list failing with a server error.
- **Fixes** detail panels on maps sitting under sticky table headers, and the tag picker list not scrolling inside dialogs.

### Upgrades

- **New units:** `danbyte-extmon-sync.timer` drives the external-monitor beat PRTG runs on, and `danbyte-scripts` also runs `sweep_deploy_pipelines` every minute. `make install-services` and the upgrade install both.
- **Site roles gain the new types:** existing site viewer and editor roles cover cooling sources, feeds, intakes and outflows, installed software and applications, application groups, PRTG rows, device profiles, rooms, location types, floor plan areas, walls and cable routes, policy rules and RPKI caches, unless an admin removed a type from the role.
- **django-rq and django-taggit** bring one small migration each.
